criterion: the boat PE expands the trailer count on the calibration turnover (item 5)
observed: tau_boat_prior_mu resolved to 3.030 from 'calibration (trailer_mean_per_visit, n = 61)' (metric trailer_mean_per_visit)
threshold: a number near 3.0 from the overlap calibration, not 1.2
why: Until 2026-09-08 the PE expanded on the retired 1.2 while the BSS learned ~2.6 through tau_bar, so the boat PE-vs-BSS gap (3,709 vs 11,118 effort) was two turnovers disagreeing, not two estimators. The PE is the design-based cross-check and now is one.

criterion: the boat turnover prior centre (item 3)
observed: lognormal(log 3.030, 0.50); shared_tau_sigma 0.15
threshold: centre 2.7-3.3 (the 61-day overlap gave 3.03 mean-per-visit), sigma 0.5
why: The previous prior lognormal(log 1.2, 0.3) sat 3+ prior SDs below the calibration and shrank tau_bar by 13% (posterior 2.60 vs likelihood-only 2.97). Re-centring removes the shrinkage; R2 measures what that does to the boat.

criterion: the crabbing-fraction classification stream exists (item 1)
threshold: hundreds of contacts, strongly seasonal (0.9+ in winter, ~0.3 in summer)
why: These rows were always in the interview workbook and were dropped by the reader's crabbers > 0 filter. They are the f data: R3a and R3 read them.

criterion: the shore turnover at the count hours (item 2; R4 adopts it)
observed: tau_shore 2.477 (peak-based 1.669) over 40 I/E days, bootstrap log-SE 0.044, weekday 2.47 / weekend 2.48
threshold: about 2.5 against the 1.7 prior in use
why: The shore counts are taken at 9:00-14:00, when presence is ~0.7 of the daily peak, so the peak-based 1.7 under-expands the count. This is the largest single mover in the series (shore x ~1.47) and it ships OFF until R4 shows what it does.

criterion: the commercial CENSUS and the charter EXPANSION, separated (item 4, settled 2026-09-09; the charter corrected 2026-09-11)
observed: total 8,538 = commercial 6,405 (census, census_expansion = 'none': 164 vessel-trips on 47 tally days, 23 unsampled calendar days at zero; per-vessel mean over 141 interviews, SE 123 = 1.9%, not carried) + charter 2,133 (expansion over the roster trip frame, vessel: 34 trips, 20 interviewed = 59%, 1,286 crab observed, SE 73 = 3.4%, CARRIED). Charter alternatives: 2,186 pooled, 1,479 on the tally frame. Baseline 11,821 under the 2026-09-08 day-type expansion of the whole component.
threshold: the commercial part is the tally-day sum with no carried error; the charter part is an expansion whose SE enters the port interval
why: Matt 2026-09-09: samplers are scheduled on the days the commercial (recreational) vessels are confirmed to be operating, so a window day without a tally is a day with no commercial fishing. Matt 2026-09-11: that census-without-error statement applies to the COMMERCIAL boats only; the charter vessels are not 100% sampled and need expansion. The charter trip roster is the frame, and on 2024-25 a quarter of its sailed trips fell on days the tally never saw.

criterion: the crabbing-holiday calendar gained Thanksgiving Day, Veterans Day (observed) and Juneteenth (2026-09-11)
observed: 13 holiday(s) in the window, 9 of them on a weekday (so they re-type a day); day types: 252 weekday, 100 weekend, 13 holiday of 365
threshold: three more days per season carry the weekend + holiday effort effects (B1 + B2) in the BSS
why: The three were added on the samplers' own Holiday? flag and the Float 20 gear count against the same month's weekday mean (Thanksgiving 2.4x, Veterans Day observed 2.3x, Juneteenth 1.7-2.3x). In the PE, an unsampled holiday in a week with no other sampled holiday lands in an EMPTY (week x day-type) stratum, which the shipped pe_empty_effort_stratum = 'zero' expands at ZERO effort: that is why the 2024-25 PE port total falls 0.5% when the three are added. The BSS imputes those days from B1 + B2 and does not have the problem. See CHANGE_REGISTER D19.

criterion: the combo-trip share c is observed from the contacts' trip types (item 1, 2026-09-09)
threshold: none in Dec-Feb, half or more in the salmon and bottomfish months
why: c does not move the boat total (f does); it is what OSP's crabbing-only count reads low by, so f(1 - c) is the prediction of that column and the comparison, when OSP delivers it, is the check of the shift-time contacts against an all-day count. In summer more than half the crabbing boats are combos, which is why OSP's column could never have identified f alone.

criterion: which interviews are the f classification: launch sites (shipped) vs launches + docks vs all
threshold: the summer months differ (docks are finfish-heavy, the marina is crab-only moorage); the protocol decides
why: Order in each triple: launches / launches+docks / all. The trailer and OSP counts measure boats launched at the ramp. A private boat interviewed at the docks is either a trailered boat that stopped to unload (then it belongs in the classification and excluding it biases f up in summer) or a moored boat (then it is outside the counted population). The marina rows are crab-only moorage boats either way. crab_fraction_contact_areas selects the set.

criterion: sampler shift coverage of the day's boat returns (item 1, shift times)
observed: 199 shift days; in port 09:44 to 15:52 (medians), 6.1 h; 75% of a day's boat returns inside the shift (all boat-I/E sites pooled (WBL has 5 days, floor 10)), 15% after the last check-out; crabbing share of typed contacts by hour: 08-10 0.54 (n=28), 10-12 0.42 (n=90), 12-14 0.43 (n=101), 14-16 0.58 (n=79), 16-18 0.50 (n=2)
threshold: flat crabbing share across the hours inside the shift; the share of returns outside it is the exposure
why: The contacts classify the boats returning during the shift. Inside it the trip-type mix does not drift with the hour (2024-25), which is the evidence available today; the returns outside the shift are unclassified and only OSP's all-day count can say whether their mix differs. shift_coverage_*.csv and contact_hour_by_trip_type.csv carry the detail.

criterion: the PE's unsampled-cell settings, all four arms on the real 2024-25 inputs (D19; the CPUE half found 2026-09-12)
observed: effort zero, CPUE pooled (through 2026-09-11): catch 72,224 (+0.0% vs the retired arm), effort 45,175; effort day_type, CPUE local: catch 81,160 (+12.4% vs the retired arm), effort 53,846; effort local_day_type, CPUE pooled: catch 90,861 (+25.8% vs the retired arm), effort 56,793; effort local_day_type, CPUE local (SHIPPED): catch 85,076 (+17.8% vs the retired arm), effort 56,793
threshold: the shipped arm is the one the fitted rungs use; the spread between arms is the size of the D19 question
why: The 2026-09-11 figure for this was +26% on the PE port total, and it was WRONG in a specific way: it paired a month-local EFFORT fill with a sub-season-pooled CPUE, so the seasonal gradient was counted once in the effort and once more in the rate. The imputed boat cells are in the summer and the pooled boat CPUE is dominated by the high-CPUE winter. Putting both halves on the month scale takes the boat all-gear PE from 42,841 to 37,018 and the port total from 90,861 to 85,076, +17.8% on the retired 72,224. Read the arm spread against R4's BSS, not against 20260904 A1, which predates the derived shore turnover and the boat recentring.

criterion: how much of the PE rests on 0 or 1 sampled days, and what that does to its SE (D21)
observed: shore_ring_net_only: 1 of 24 cells unsampled (1 days) and 10 singleton (19 days) = 26% of days; SE 550 vs 238 on the retired arithmetic; shore_all_gear: 21 of 93 cells unsampled (45 days) and 37 singleton (82 days) = 44% of days; SE 1,379 vs 410 on the retired arithmetic; private_boat_ring_net_only: 6 of 24 cells unsampled (11 days) and 7 singleton (14 days) = 33% of days; SE 79 vs 29 on the retired arithmetic; private_boat_all_gear: 23 of 93 cells unsampled (48 days) and 34 singleton (77 days) = 43% of days; SE 1,310 vs 573 on the retired arithmetic
threshold: the SE must widen when half the days rest on one observation or none
why: The retired SE was sqrt(N^2 sd^2 / max(n,1)) with sd from the cell's own sampled days, and sd() of ONE observation is NA, replaced by 0. So 37 of 93 shore all-gear cells and 34 of 93 boat cells contributed their full point estimate and no variance, and so did every imputed cell: the shore SE was bit-identical at 410 whether the fill added 0 or 7,947 effort units. This is a PE-side interval, but a gate-failed component reports its PE point in the port total as a CONSTANT, which is the case where it reaches the headline. pe_variance = 'sampled_only' restores the old arithmetic exactly.

criterion: gear shares by trip-level bootstrap (item 6)
threshold: intervals several times wider than the retired Dirichlet on crab counts
why: Crab arrive in trips, not one at a time; the Dirichlet(catch + 0.5) treated every crab as an independent draw. The report now applies per-population x sub-season shares.

criterion: item 8 + the new f: the SHORE against the baseline (the boat is expected to move with f)
observed: shore pc 6,343 (+0.4%), shore ag 21,502 (+0.1%), boat pc 1,070 (+5.1%), boat ag 43,668 (+40.8%); census 7,884 (baseline 11,821: exact over the tally days by design)
threshold: both shore components within a few percent; the boat rises with the winter f (no threshold)
why: The hours filter dropped 22 boat trips (14 with recorded catch) and ~140 shore rows whose time field was blank or under 0.5 h; under the deployment unit a set pot with zero time is real effort with real catch. Restoring them lowers the boat CPUE slightly (more zeros) and barely moves the shore. The rebuilt workbook (2026-09-09) also applies the tampered-gear filter (13 Grays Harbor interviews in 2024-25) and a few source corrections. The census is not compared: it is now the exact sum over the tally days (-3,869 by design). UNDER new_throughout the boat ALSO carries the dynamic monthly f, whose winter months run 0.88 to 1.00 against the retired 0.30 anchor, so the boat moving several tens of percent here is the design and not a regression. The f change is not attributed by any fit in this mode; add R2f for the factorization proof or run F_METHOD = 'ladder' for the full attribution.

criterion: the boat turnover under the pre-patch prior (the R2 control)
observed: tau_bar 2.6117 (baseline 2.6130)
threshold: about 2.6: the calibration says ~3.0 and the 1.2 prior is pulling it down
why: This is the number R2 exists to move.

criterion: the shore did not move (the boat prior cannot reach it)
observed: shore fits vs R1: 6270 shared parameter rows across 4 summaries identical at full precision; configs differ in 5 key(s): shared_tau_sigma, tau_boat_prior_calibration_table, tau_boat_prior_mu, tau_boat_prior_sigma, tau_boat_prior_source
threshold: shore fits bit-identical to R1
why: A FAIL means the turnover prior leaked into the shore fits, which it has no path to do.

criterion: tau_bar lands on the calibration and the boat rises with it
threshold: tau_bar 2.8-3.1; boat all-gear +10 to +18%
why: Effort = lambda_E x tau x f, so the boat moves in proportion to tau_bar. Likelihood-only tau was 2.97 against the shrunk posterior 2.60, i.e. +14%; the OSP series identifies tau_bar and the prior should no longer fight it. A move outside 8-20% means something else changed.

criterion: boat PPC still calibrated after the prior move
threshold: PIT means near 0.5, coverage near nominal
why: The prior move should improve, not worsen, the OSP stream's fit: read the OSP/trailer rows.

criterion: the shore did not move when f was rolled back (f is boat-only)
observed: shore fits, R2f vs R2: 6270 shared parameter rows across 4 summaries identical at full precision; configs differ in 4 key(s): crab_fraction_dynamic, crab_fraction_rows, crab_fraction_source, crab_fraction_strata
threshold: shore fits bit-identical to R2
why: crab_fraction_stan_data() sets apply_crab_fraction = 0 for shore; a FAIL means an f term reached the shore.

criterion: the f block leaves effort and CPUE untouched (factorization)
observed: boat non-f parameters, R2f vs R2: 1957 shared rows across 2 summaries; max |z| 3.20 (private_boat_ring_net_only_Dungeness_Kept:L_raw[13]); 2 rows above 3 (0.10%)
threshold: max |z| under 5 and under 1% of rows above 3
why: This is the R3-vs-R3a test of the 2026-09-08 design, run as a single control rung against the CURRENT turnover prior instead of the retired one. A FAIL means an f term reached an effort or CPUE likelihood, which would make every boat number in the ladder attributable to two things at once.

criterion: what the new f is worth on the boat, at a fixed turnover
observed: boat all-gear with the new f 45,604 vs the retired f 33,641 (+35.6%); shore unchanged
threshold: informational: this is the f effect the 'ladder' mode spends two fits to attribute
why: The boat is linear in f day by day, so this ratio is the effort-weighted change in f. Read it against crab_fraction_strata_*.csv from the R2 folder, which carries the monthly f the walk produced and the contact counts behind each month.

criterion: the boat did not move (the shore prior cannot reach it)
observed: boat fits vs R3: 4170 shared parameter rows across 4 summaries identical at full precision; configs differ in 7 key(s): census_uncertainty, charter_expansion, charter_frame, shared_tau_min_obs, tau_shore_prior_mu, tau_shore_prior_sigma, tau_shore_prior_source  <-- 3 UNEXPECTED: census_uncertainty, charter_expansion, charter_frame
threshold: boat fits bit-identical to the previous rung
why: A FAIL means the shore turnover leaked into the boat fits, which it has no path to do.

criterion: the shore scales by the ratio of the two turnovers
observed: shore all-gear effort 34,837 vs 25,683 (x1.356); catch 29,210 vs 21,502 (x1.358); pot closure catch 8,963 vs 6,343 (x1.413)
threshold: about x1.45 (2.48 / 1.7), effort and catch alike, both sub-seasons
why: The shore is linear in tau_shore; the derived prior is 2.48 against 1.7 and the shared level carries it. A ratio well off 1.45 means the data (I/E trips) pulled the level, which is worth reading: the I/E stream is the only shore observation that can.

criterion: the I/E observation scale did not worsen
threshold: not larger than R3's
why: If the I/E trips disagree with the derived turnover, sigma_IE absorbs the disagreement; it should not grow.

criterion: the port total with the derived shore turnover
threshold: informational; the decision (adopt, or hold for a field check) is Matt's
why: A paired gear count on every I/E day is the cheap field confirmation of the derived turnover.

criterion: the two tracks agree on the R4 configuration
observed: gear port 93,274 vs pooled 94,376 (-1.17%); boat all-gear gear 45,374 vs pooled 45,604; shore all-gear gear 28,334 vs pooled 29,210
threshold: within about 2% at the port
why: Two independently parameterized CPUE structures fitting the same data. The gear track's shore all-gear fit sits at monthly and its catch likelihood is plain NB2, so a small standing gap is expected (about -0.8% on 2026-09-05); a large one after these patches points at the boat.

criterion: the shared turnover agrees across tracks
observed: gear tau_bar 2.9766 vs pooled 2.9771 (-0.02%)
threshold: within a few percent
why: tau_bar is a property of the OSP/trailer data; the two tracks estimated it to 0.03% on 2026-09-01.

criterion: the dynamic f agrees across tracks (it reads the same contacts)
observed: max |f_gear - f_pooled| over months 0.002
threshold: under 0.03
why: The f block is identical in both Stan files and reads the same rows; a gap here is a data-plumbing bug, not a model difference.
